selection_rule: Choose the role from content and verbal tone, not from a house-style default. Across a multi-image set, vary the display skeleton when the subjects differ; preserve one coherent hierarchy inside each image.

roles.name: Literary
roles.display: characterful old-style, transitional, or soft editorial serif; roman or italic

roles.name: Cultural Grotesk
roles.display: wide geometric or neo-grotesk with assertive custom spacing
behavior: letters may touch or optically interlock
one word may span the page

roles.name: Condensed Civic
behavior: facts align to one strong edge

roles.name: Programmatic
roles.display: medium grotesk or engineered modular sans
roles.support: tabular numerals, mono, or narrow information face
behavior: dates and numerals may become the anchor

roles.name: Rotated Display
roles.display: serif or grotesk selected for strong letter silhouettes
behavior: one title rotates 90 degrees or runs vertically

roles.name: Handwritten Interjection
roles.display: human handwritten phrase, quick script, or dry marker note used as a secondary voice
roles.support: clean sans or serif carries all factual information
behavior: one circled note or crossing phrase
never used for dates or essential facts

roles.name: Typographic Object
roles.display: oversized serif, grotesk, or abstracted letterforms chosen for the word shape
behavior: one word may leave the page
letters may split around or overprint the subject

secondary_voice_rules: Use one primary display skeleton per image; do not combine multiple novelty display faces.
A handwritten voice is optional and secondary, limited to one short phrase or annotation.
Choose at most one orientation event: rotated title, vertical stack, interlocked word, or handwritten interruption.
Within a multi-image series, consistency comes from ink, spacing, plate logic, and microtype discipline; display fonts may change with the content.
Never reproduce distinctive lettering, wording, or exact line breaks from a reference image.
